поїздів.Інші структурні підрозділи Укрзалізниці беруть участь у роботі з питань безпеки руху поїздів згідно з функціональними обов'язками.Ключові слова: транспорт,

title: Towards the Automation of the Production of Railway Safety Cases
abstract: This paper outlines a research project being carried out by the University of Birmingham, in collaboration with four industrial partners, sponsored by the UK LINK Inland Surface Transport Programme. The primary objective of the project is to progress automation of the production of safety cases for the railway industry. It has commenced with an investigation of current practice and the requirements of an automation tool for the production of safety cases. This paper outlines the project programme, reviews the investigation results, examines key issues in the production processes, and briefly discusses a generic model of safety case production which was developed as a common platform for further study and to develop and assess requirements for the automation tool.

title: Railway Safety Supervision and Management Information System
abstract: A unified information sharing platform for railway safety supervision and management has been established in the Ministry of Railways and Railway Bureau by integrating and accessing the existing matured information of safety monitoring and alarming,manual inspection,and accident investigation analysis.The information sharing platform can realize the three-tier networking and safety information sharing among the Ministry of Railways,Railway Bureau and station depot for railway safety supervision and management,provide the integrated management of safety information,analysis and decision-making and information service.Through four closed loop management,including the disposal of the monitoring and alarming information,the safety inspection information,the investigation and analysis of accident,and the comprehensive analysis and judgement,the safety dynamic of the whole railway system is mastered.Railway safety supervision and management become more real-time,targeted and effective to form a more systematic,network-based,information-based railway safety inspection and monitoring guarantee system.The key technologies for developing railway safety supervision and management information system include the optimization of core business processes,information sharing platform technology,optimizing the organization of data resources,interface program and interface standards of relevant professional safety monitoring system data,safety early warning analysis and assistant decision-making technology,etc.

title: PROBLEMS OF RELIABILITY IN THE USE OF MICRO-ELECTRONICS IN RAILWAY SAFETY TECHNIQUES
abstract: The next generation of railway safety installations will be based on microelectronics. In view of relay techniques, new switching and other methods will have to be found. Problems are discussed, taking as an example reliability in information processing and an accommodation circuit for optic signalling.

title: ADVANCED-DATA ACQUISITION AND AUTOMATED MONITORING SYSTEMS IN RAILWAY SAFETY
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF RESEARCH IN COMPUTER APPLICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
abstract: Advanced data acquisition and automated monitoring systems represent a transformative advancement in railway safety and operational efficiency.Integrating sophisticated train control technologies, TETRA protocols, and nanosensor implementations has revolutionized track maintenance and safety protocols.Through the deployment of multi-tiered monitoring frameworks incorporating ultrasonic B-scan detection, RFID tracking, and mobile inspection platforms, railway networks have achieved enhanced defect detection capabilities and improved resource utilization.Implementing machine learning algorithms and real-time data processing has enabled proactive maintenance strategies, while integrated GPR and InSAR technologies have strengthened track inspection capabilities.These technological advancements have Sridevi Palepu

title: A study of China's railway safety supervision system
journal: Technology and Economy in Areas of Communications
abstract: It firstly analyzes the present situation of railway safety management in China,and then points out the weakness in the existing safety supervision system.At last,on the basis of the reference of foreign experience,it presents the corresponding measures so that China's railway can fully face more security challenges.

title: Present Development of Software for Railway Safety
abstract: Railway is Cyber-Physical System (CPS), which is distributed over a large territory. It requires secure communication not only among various parts of system, but also with operation center. Building its own communication networks by the railway system operator is financially demanding, which is why more or less open communication systems are used. This is connected with higher requirements for the security of applications, operated in a CPS. European project COSMSOS has been creating a tool that applies DevOps development technologies from the IT field to the field of embedded systems, to which railway system belong. The article shows that this very complex software must be adapted to real requirements, which are put on railway operation system safety.

title: Discussion on Application of Railway Safety Evaluation Method
abstract: Safety risk management is aiming at the safety problem in people's production and life, it used to reduce and control dangerous and harmful factors in process of production, as well as each production accident. Based on expounding the concept and role of safety evaluation, this paper analyzes safety evaluation methods in each stage of railway construction and operation, such as safety pre-evaluation, safety acceptance evaluation and safety status evaluation, discusses the application of safety evaluation on railway safety risk management and puts forward the application scope of the evaluation, all of these provide management approaches and technical support for railways implementing risk management.

title: Study on Design of Railway Safety Siding
abstract: Safety siding,an important safety facility of railway and one of the major measures to guarantee the safety of railway transportation,must be designed in conformity with the national standards.At present,our rail transport is composed of systems with various types and grades,such as normal speed railway,intercity railway,high-speed railway etc.As trains drive at different speeds and safety sidings are diversified in location,each safety siding should be designed in accordance with its alone function and role,and with different design method and content.Modification on safety siding standards is also proposed to adapt the new security requirement so as to ensure the safety of railway operation.

title: NEXT GENERATION RAILWAY SAFETY: IOT COLLISION AVOIDANCE TECHNOLOGY
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
authors: T. Durga, G. Aasha, J. Monisha & V. Sangeetha
abstract: Railway transportation plays a vital role in public and freight transport. However, train collisions caused by human error, signal failure, and track damage continue to pose serious safety risks. This project presents an IoT-based Train Collision Avoidance System designed to detect potential collision scenarios and prevent accidents in real time. The proposed system uses sensors such as ultrasonic sensors, GPS modules, and IoT-enabled microcontrollers to continuously monitor train position, track conditions, and obstacles. Sensor data is transmitted wirelessly to a centralized control system using IoT communication technologies. When a potential collision or abnormal condition is detected, alerts are sent to the driver and control room, and automatic braking mechanisms can be activated. The system aims to reduce human dependency, enhance railway safety, and minimize loss of life and property. The proposed solution is cost-effective, scalable, and suitable for modern smart railway infrastructure.

title: Railway Safety Perspectives: Trends, Concerns and Future Directions
journal: International Journal of Intelligent Systems and Applications in Engineering
abstract: Rail transport has significantly transformed human mobility, and with its continuous development, the focus on train and infrastructure safety—particularly concerning passengers—has become increasingly critical. This paper examines the various methods adopted to ensure high levels of safety in railways through an extensive review of existing literature. A total of 48 relevant articles were shortlisted for in-depth analysis, combining bibliometric research with a comprehensive literature assessment to evaluate current safety management practices in the railway sector. In recent years, high-speed rail systems have drawn considerable attention from experts and railway authorities due to their higher risk potential. Consequently, numerous advanced technologies, supported by artificial intelligence and machine learning, are being developed worldwide to guarantee consistently high safety standards. Among the most sensitive areas are railway stations, especially platform zones, which represent critical hotspots for accidents, including suicide incidents. Various preventive strategies have demonstrated measurable improvements in safety, reinforcing railways as one of the safest modes of transport infrastructure. Building on these advancements, the application of resilient safety models could further strengthen safety performance and ensure more robust protection for passengers and operations.

title: Establishing the Relationship between Railway Safety & Operational Performance
journal: University of Birmingham Research Portal (University of Birmingham)
abstract: Deregulation and/or privatisation of railway systems has been adopted in many developed countries, aimed at improving economic performance. Literature on railway performance mainly focuses on the effects of reforms and on liberalization itself as well as measuring performance indicators for the management of assets in the railway industry. Although these management reforms on the maintenance and operations of rail infrastructures are generally found to have contributed to improving trends of rail safety and safety performance, there is not much evidence from research to support this. There is also little work on how the lessons from restructuring can apply in developing countries. Identifying approaches that can revitalize railways in developing and emerging economies while raising standards of safety and operational performance is the objective of this paper. Presented are some of the specific lessons from developed countries and how they can be applied in developing economies’ railways, noting that it is not generally feasible to adopt best practices because of social and or economic constraints. Only where there is a significant foreign investor is there the potential to replicate best in class technology and operational practices, so the presentation will identify areas where less well funded railways can adopt lessons from developed countries – using both historical and current international benchmarks. The originality of this approach lies in establishing the relationship between performance and safety in the era of reforms and liberalization of the rail industry. The paper analyses publicly available data to suggest how rail safety considerations have impacted in a more general way upon railway performance and by extension, derive lessons for emerging and developing economies.

title: NEXT GENERATION RAILWAY SAFETY: IOT COLLISION AVOIDANCE TECHNOLOGY
